subject: Cloud Computing
title: GitOps: Infrastructure from Git
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on GitOps: Infrastructure from Git.

hook.text: What if your entire infrastructure was defined in a Git repository, and every merge deployed automatically?

buildup.text: GitOps uses Git as the single source of truth for infrastructure and application state.

discovery.text: Tools like ArgoCD and Flux watch the repo and automatically sync the cluster to match what's in Git.

twist.text: Every change goes through a pull request. That means code review, audit trails, and easy rollbacks — for infrastructure.

climax.text: GitOps brings software engineering practices to infrastructure. It's version control for your entire cloud.

punchline.text: If it's not in Git, it doesn't exist. That's GitOps.

quiz.question: What is the core principle of GitOps?
options: Git is the single source of truth and changes automatically sync to infrastructure
All Git repositories must be hosted on GitHub specifically
Infrastructure changes are made manually and then documented in Git

details.summary: GitOps uses Git as the single source of truth for both application and infrastructure state. Changes are made via pull requests, and automated agents reconcile the live environment with the desired state declared in the repository.
details.whyItMatters: GitOps brings the rigor of code review and version control to infrastructure operations. Every change is auditable, reversible, and approved before it reaches production.
takeaways: Git is the single source of truth for desired state
Automated agents reconcile live state with the repository
Every change is auditable through Git history

faq.question: How does GitOps differ from traditional CI/CD?
faq.answer: Traditional CI/CD pushes changes to the environment after build. GitOps pulls desired state from Git and continuously reconciles. The environment converges toward what is declared in Git, even if someone makes manual changes that drift from the declared state.

faq.question: What tools implement GitOps?
faq.answer: ArgoCD and Flux are the most popular GitOps operators for Kubernetes. They watch Git repositories and automatically apply changes to clusters. Both support multi-cluster management, progressive delivery, and integration with secret management tools.
